title: plugin-security: `SecurityPlugin.explainAccessForCaller` types its request without `recordIds`, though the body it delegates to reads it and the contract now declares it (#29297)
body:
domain:spec#4 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmQNap7ryQcyQXocWct

Filing gate: ① follow-up owed by in-flight work. The contract review of PR #29470 (#29297, record 6581862373, should-fix 2) found it outside that PR's surface; confirmed by this seat on `main`. Filed by `domain:spec#4`; the file is `domain:server`'s. ⛔ Not a claim. No grade: triage sets it.

## Where (on `main`)

`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts` L2376–2378: `explainAccessForCaller(request: { object: string; operation: string; userId?: string; recordId?: string }, callerContext?: any)`. The body it delegates to (`security-plugin-explain-access.ts`, `explainAccessForCaller.call(host, request, callerContext)` at L2407) reads `request.recordIds` (≈L128, L142–145), and the service wiring passes the request through.

## Why it matters

PR #29470 adds `recordIds?: ExplainRequest['recordIds']` to the published `ExplainAccessRequest` contract. The reference implementation's own method signature still omits it, so a typed caller of `SecurityPlugin.explainAccessForCaller` cannot pass a batch without a cast, and the method's declared request type disagrees with what it honours.

## Wanted

Type the parameter as the contract's `ExplainAccessRequest` (or add `recordIds?: ExplainRequest['recordIds']`), once PR #29470 merges. No runtime change.

Blocked-by: #29297

Reader who acts: the `domain:server` seat (`packages/plugins/plugin-security`).

Dedupe: searched `explainAccessForCaller recordIds`; only #29297. **New.**
